mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In the specified regime, 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the pre-rate hike period (p > 0.1) or the rate hike is reversed before the 60-day horizon.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL prints above 208.0 for three consecutive months, it indicates accelerating price pressures that the S&P 500 anticipates by adjusting upward expected discount rates, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 208.0 and remains above for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over the trigger period, 20-day forward returns are positive or non-negative (p < 0.05) or CPIAUCSL reverts before the 20-day window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS exceeding 2% from the prior month coincides with increased hiring momentum that boosts corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by more than 2% from the prior month
failure_condition: In strengthening labor markets, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.1) or hiring decelerates before the 5-day window.

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO falls below 115.0 for two consecutive months, it signals supply-side contraction that outpaces demand, causing the S&P 500 to price in lower future growth and produce negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 115.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During supply contraction regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly negative (p > 0.1) or INDPRO recovers before the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST above 1400 units for three months reflects strengthening demand for consumer goods, which the market interprets as a positive signal for S&P 500 valuation expansion and 60-day positive returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by more than 100 units each month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In robust demand regimes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 60-day average (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in UNRATE below 4.0% and a two-month drop in GDPC1 above 11500 suggest dual headwinds: lower wage growth and weaker demand, jointly depressing discount rates and producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% AND GDPC1 > 11500 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) or the proxies move in opposite directions during the trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A steady upward trend in the 5-week moving average of RSAFS above 380,000 for 10 consecutive weeks indicates improving credit conditions that the market anticipates by pricing in higher corporate optimism and 20-day positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.1) or the 5-week RSAFS trend reverses before the window.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE falls below 4.0% for three consecutive months in a non-recession regime, it signals weaker wage growth expectations that the market incorporates into lower equity discounting, producing negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.0% for three consecutive months and current regime is not recession
failure_condition: In the specified regime, 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.1) or UNRATE recovers before the horizon.
